newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Mboweni expects agreement on labour bill.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Mboweni expects agreement on labour bill.

text.p: Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Wednesday he was optimistic that controversial new labour legislation would be presented to parliament by September 15.

Addressing a news briefing after meetings with business and union leaders on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, Mboweni described the talks as "extremely" difficult, but said there were areas where the two sides could find consensus.
"There were some hard issues on the table but they have been narrowed and focused and I am certain we will be able to reach some accommodation before September 15," Mboweni said.
"I am confident we will reach sufficient agreement for the parties to support the bill to go to parliament."
Mboweni said signs of the improved prospects of a settlement were that areas of disagreement had narrowed and that further meetings would be held within the next two weeks.

He added that government was currently involved in bilateral consulations with labour and business, but that there was a possibility of proposing three-way meetings, between labour, business and the government.
Labour has refused to meet face to face with business unless it radically revises its position on the bill.
The proposed law, was approved by the cabinet in April but still has to passed by parliament before it can take effect.

It has been the subject of ongoing clashes between labour and business, with the Congress of South African Trade Unions staging a one-day national work stoppage on June 2 to press business to revise its position.

The labour federation has threatened fresh national strikes in August to reinforce its demands for a 40-hour working week to be phased in over not more than five years, six months' maternity leave of which at least four are paid and double pay for Sunday work.
Business is concerned about the bill's wide scope and provisions which could raise employment costs to the point of creating obstacles to new jobs.
